step-1.text: Stand one side panel on its edge, holes facing in. Screw in eight cam pins by hand, then tap in eight dowels.

count-1.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 8 cam pins and 8 wood dowels.

step-2.text: Push the bottom panel onto the low pins and dowels. Drop two cam locks into the round holes, arrows facing the pins, and turn them clockwise until they grab.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 bottom panel and 2 cam locks.

step-3.text: The fixed shelves hold the bookcase square, so they go in now. Slide onto the pins and lock with cam locks, clockwise.

count-3.text: This step uses 3 fixed shelves and 6 cam locks.

step-4.text: Pins and dowels go into the ends of the panels on this side too. With a helper, lower the second side onto all of them at once, then lock the last eight cam locks.

count-4.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 8 cam pins, 8 wood dowels and 8 cam locks.

step-5.text: Tap four dowels into the top edges of the sides. Set the top panel on, good side up, then lock it from inside with four cam locks.

count-5.text: This step uses 1 top panel, 4 wood dowels and 4 cam locks.

step-6.text: Roll the bookcase over so it lies on its front. Ask your helper, and put the flattened box underneath to save the finish.

count-6.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-7.text: Lay the back panel on, smooth side facing in. Line it up with one corner and nail it along the edges, about every twenty centimeters. If the corners line up, the bookcase is square.

step-8.text: Stand it up together. Lift with your legs, not your back.

count-8.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-9.text: Last step, and the most important. Screw the wall bracket to the top at the back, then fix it to the wall with screws that suit your wall. Furniture can tip over. Always anchor it.

done.text: Done. Your HODEDAH 4-shelf bookcase is built. Give it a proud little pat.
